goals: mechanistic: characterize elevation- and soil-controlled runoff generation and snowmelt timing across the Naches
validation: compare aggregated basin water yield to the American River gauge (feasible only at monthly/seasonal scale, not daily NSE as posed)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves per-point water balance and snow across the elevation/soil gradient; NLDAS gives elevation-varying forcing. It cannot route to a gauge.

answerable: elevation/soil control on runoff generation and ET partitioning per column
snowmelt timing and peak-SWE per elevation band (H2OSNO/QSNOMELT in default output)
aggregated basin water YIELD at monthly/seasonal scale via area-weighted summation of column runoff

not_answerable.aspect: daily streamflow hydrograph at the gauge and its NSE (the stated deliverable)
not_answerable.why: single-column ELM has NO lateral transport or channel routing; there is no native integrated streamflow, and daily NSE is dominated by routing-controlled timing/recession the stack cannot reproduce

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil), with runoff aggregation for validation
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x 2 dominant soil classes = 6 cells, x2 light replication to capture within-band forcing spread from distinct NLDAS cells (~15 precip values at this relief) and soil variability = 12. Smallest design that spans the rain-snow gradient and the soil partitioning control while enabling an area-weighted yield estimate.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample the mid-elevation rain-snow transition where melt timing controls seasonal yield; concentrate replicates where NLDAS cell boundaries and soil contrasts coincide; ensure each band's area weight is represented for aggregation.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 per stratum cell to sample distinct NLDAS forcing cells and soil sub-variability within each band.

sampling_plan.reason: rain-dominated fast runoff on well-drained soil; sets warm-season low-flow behavior.
isolates soil partitioning (more ET/less drainage) under valley forcing.
melt-timing-controlled runoff on drained soil; the dominant seasonal-yield lever.
melt plus fine-soil retention; tests transition-zone partitioning.
snow accumulation/melt-dominated yield; note ridgetop SWE underestimation from 12 km cells.
high-band soil control on meltwater partitioning.

validation_design.target_variable: basin water yield (area-weighted sum of column QRUNOFF)
validation_design.observation_source: USGS gauge: American River nr Nile (daily discharge)
validation_design.comparison: aggregated — sum column runoff x band area weights to a basin flux, then compare at MONTHLY/SEASONAL scale (daily comparison is invalid without routing)
validation_design.metric: monthly bias and volume error; seasonal correlation. NSE on the daily hydrograph is NOT computable with current capability.

validation_design.observation_source: SNOTEL (if a station falls in-basin — not listed in brief)
validation_design.comparison: analog — process check against nearest SNOTEL if available; expect ridgetop underestimation

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 default forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff routing / hydrograph aggregation (column runoff -> channel network -> gauge daily discharge)
requires_capabilities.why: single-column ELM produces no integrated streamflow; daily NSE requires routed timing
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire stated deliverable (daily hydrograph + NSE)

requires_capabilities.why: needed to area-weight column runoff into a basin-integrated flux above the gauge
requires_capabilities.blocks: even the monthly/seasonal yield fallback comparison

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS gauge daily-discharge ingest + drainage-area metadata
requires_capabilities.why: to align modeled yield with the observed series and correct for contributing area
to validate snowmelt timing that drives seasonal yield
requires_capabilities.blocks: confidence in the snow-driven runoff mechanism

assumptions: Naches is within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 elevation-varying forcing applies (default).
Dominant soil classes will be derived downstream from SSURGO; exact classes not provided.
A short run per column is available as the WTD-warm-start carrier state.
The gauge's contributing area is a sub-basin of HUC 17030002, not the whole HUC — aggregation must respect the gauge's drainage area.
open_questions: Is a daily NSE strictly required, or is a monthly/seasonal volume-and-timing skill acceptable given no routing?
Is any routing/aggregation step (even a simple linear-reservoir or unit-hydrograph post-processor) permissible to build?
What is the exact drainage area above the American River nr Nile gauge, and does it match the bbox?
Are any in-basin SNOTEL stations available for snow validation?
